civilopediaText.text: The fall of Ilythiir marked the end of the Dark Age. - Ardour the Old

Also known as the Time of Beginnings, the Restoration Age began in the first year of the Human-created solar calendar, which eventually replaced the Elven lunar calendar. During this age, the Gods decided to erase the memories of Earth's inhabitants, leaving only a few with any recollection of the past. They also populated the Earth with many new speaking peoples, taught them essential survival skills, and allowed them to develop independently. The Gods agreed to limit their intervention on Earth, especially after their significant interference to end the Age of Demons, which had led to the Dark Age.

People discover traces of aether—a raw, ancient force embedded in the world’s ley lines and hidden within the earth itself. The sheer potential of aether, hinted in ancient texts and runic carvings, sparks a fevered age of exploration and experiments. Scholar across races dedicate themselves to uncovering and harnessing its power, refining it into mana to perform magic. They see the once-mysterious force as a means to unlock boundless power, yet its true nature remains elusive. But the thirst for knowledge propels society forward, setting the stage for mastery of magic and the reawakening of long-dormant arts.

As mana studies flourish, the world enters a period of intellectual and spiritual awakening. Mages and scholars begin to understand the intricate relationships between aether, mana, and spells. Academies arise to teach young minds in the arts of magic, and what was once the privilege of an elite few begins to spread among those with the gift. Summoning rituals are perfected, allowing the summoning of powerful heroes from other worlds to change the course of history.

name: Magi-Industry Age
uniques: Every major Civilization gains a spy once a civilization enters this era

civilopediaText.text: Artificers and magi-engineers develop standardized magical tools and mastered the forging of rune stones—stabilized mana crystals. Once limited to natural formations, rune stones can now be crafted, igniting a technological revolution. Cities are illuminated by glowing mana-powered towers, and rune-enhanced machinery transforms industry and agriculture. Society flourishes as these magical creations improve daily life, yet tensions rise with emerging power imbalances. Armies march with enchanted weaponry, fueling an ever-growing demand for rune stones.

civilopediaText.text: The discovery of Altalium -a rare, luminous mineral with unique magical properties, allows humans and other races to explore the sky. Airships become the nowest mode of transport, linking cities once separated by vast landscapes or treacherous waters. The new age brings people closer together, uniting distant lands through trade and shared cultural exchange.

civilopediaText.text: The boundaries of magic and technology blur as society reaches the pinnacle of its achievements. Mana are no longer just a mystical force; it has been weaponized and refined, used to create weapons of unparalleled power and precision. Nations wield enchanted armaments, altalium-powered airships, and magic-imbued defenses. The destructive incantation, Armageddon, causes fear because of its ability to unleash catastrophic devastation, reducing entire cities to wastelands.
